analysis.title: 13F Tearsheets - Q3 2026 vs Q2 2026: What The Smart Money Bought And Sold
key_insights: Scorecard of 19 closely watched filers across the most crowded names (SpaceX, Amazon, Alphabet, Meta, Microsoft, Nvidia, TSMC, Intel, Micron, Applied Materials, AMD, Broadcom, Seagate, Sandisk, Nebius, CoreWeave, Uber, Visa). The change in reported 13F value ranged from -92% (Situational Awareness) to +21% (Pershing Square). Pershing Square, Icahn, Paulson, Glenview and Appaloosa were among the few with a higher or roughly flat value.

Situational Awareness' 13F fell from $20.24BN to $1.58BN after the July rout. It closed 21 of 26 lines, including Sandisk ($5.67BN), Micron ($5.57BN), Bloom Energy ($1.90BN), TSMC ($1.27BN) and Nebius ($1.23BN). What remains is mostly calls (66% of reported value), led by Bloom Energy calls ($389M notional) and new Nebius calls ($333M). The filing is a Sept. 30 snapshot, before October's selloff.

Nvidia's own 13F fell from $63.44BN to $48.33BN. It cut Intel 25% (214.8M to 161.1M shares, $29.99BN to $19.37BN) and Nokia 56%, and raised SpaceX 6.3% to 130.5M shares ($19.68BN). SpaceX is now its largest position at 40.7% of the book, just ahead of Intel at 40.1%.

SpaceX (SPCX) was a crowded name with mixed flows. Tepper multiplied his stake 17x ($38M to $557M), Third Point raised it 5.4x to $148M, Nvidia added 6.3% and Druckenmiller started a $30M position. Seller side: D1 cut 9.3M shares but SpaceX is still 55% of its book ($17.61BN), Altimeter cut 41%, BlueCrest cut 94% and Viking exited.

Chip positioning diverged. Druckenmiller cut TSMC 94% and sold AMD, Sandisk, Lam, Arm and others outright, while Lone Pine moved from Applied Materials (-92%) and Seagate (sold) into TSMC (17x to $783M) and a new $721M Intel stake. Tepper added Micron (+28%, now his largest holding at $1.33BN), Nvidia (+31%), Lam (+63%) and ASML (+30%).

Memory and storage: Druckenmiller nearly tripled Seagate (+180% to $315M) with $90M of new calls and a new $37M Western Digital stake, making it his No. 2 position. Lone Pine sold $965M of Seagate and D1 sold Seagate ($29M). Discovery's top holding remains Sandisk at $373M (17% of the book).

Alphabet was cut by many filers. Tepper cut Alphabet 46%, Baupost 31%, Tiger 42% and Third Point 83%. D1 sold its Alphabet stake outright. Lone Pine raised Alphabet 10x to $743M, Viking opened a $595M position and Senator went from 10,000 to 116,138 shares.
Tesla was bought by several funds. Altimeter opened a $680M Tesla position and Viking quadrupled to $831M (2.34M shares), moving from 547,816 shares.

Berkshire Hathaway's 13F value rose to $304.2BN from $299.3BN. It cut Bank of America by 27.5M shares to 455.9M (about $1.5BN), nearly doubled Lennar Class A to 26.0M shares ($2.12BN), raised Delta 12% to 64.5M shares and added a new $689M Bending Spoons position. There were no terminations and Apple was untouched at 227.9M shares (25% of the book).

Hedging via index and sector puts: Senator more than doubled S&P 500 ETF puts to 626,000 shares ($477M notional, now its largest line). Corvex added $191M of SPY puts. Third Point raised SPY puts to $47M. Glenview added Health Care Select SPDR puts ($152M) and Russell 2000 puts ($256M) and closed SPY puts. Altimeter bought $512M notional of semiconductor ETF (SMH) puts. Soros' Energy Select SPDR puts rose to $670M notional with new XOP puts ($328M).

BlueCrest reshuffled from index ETF shorts and longs to long SPY calls. SPY calls went from $22M to $648M notional (23% of the reported book), while the equal-weight S&P ETF was cut to under $1M, the SPDR Portfolio S&P 500 ETF ($230M) was sold and SPY puts were cut 94%. It added puts on high yield (HYG $79M), financials (XLF $82M) and small caps (IWM $60M). Options are $1.48BN of its $2.76BN.

Soros bought rate and utility duration via new calls on long Treasuries (TLT, $237M notional) and utilities (XLU, $215M), multiplied Intel 28x to $340M (its largest stock holding), and exited converts and AI hardware including Lumentum notes ($208M), Super Micro preferred ($111M) and Nebius ($86M). Options are $2.03BN and converts $1.17BN of $8.51BN reported.

Druckenmiller's book shrank to $4.47BN from $5.21BN (65 lines versus 95). He sold the chip book, closed all four ETF call positions (RSP, EWZ, IWM, SPY, $487M notional) and added a gold-miner trio (Newmont, Barrick, Agnico Eagle, $129M combined). Natera is now 29% of the book.
Glenview went from 45 to 140 line items with 106 new positions. It cut CVS 73% ($499M to $110M) and Viatris 98%, and raised Onto Innovation 184%, Humana 115%, Teva 49%, Meta 39% and AMD 31%.

D1 Capital cut SpaceX 7.4% but it is still 55% of its book. It sold Meta, Alphabet, Ferguson, DoorDash and Intuitive Surgical outright, and scaled up Lattice Semiconductor (+462% to $766M), Madison Air (20x to $618M), Qnity (6x) and Martin Marietta (+290%), with new Flex ($402M) and Viking Holdings ($315M).

Viking Global turned over 36 positions (closed 36 of 79 lines), exiting Schwab ($982M), Johnson Controls, Union Pacific and Microsoft, cutting Visa 33%, and making TSMC the largest holding after a 23% increase to $1.78BN. New: Mastercard ($818M), Honeywell Aerospace ($671M), Alphabet ($595M).

Pershing Square's 13F rose to $30.80BN from $25.52BN. It cut Microsoft 35% (6.21M to 4.06M shares), opened Intercontinental Exchange ($1.01BN) and Alcon ($954M), and raised Netflix 18%. Pershing Square Inc. is 33% of the book after a price rise from $6.06BN to $10.31BN.

Icahn's 13F rose to $9.43BN from $8.26BN, driven by CVR Energy's value rising from $1.96BN to $3.63BN on an unchanged 71.2M shares. He sold JetBlue ($118M) and American Electric Power ($59M) and cut EchoStar 64%, Bausch + Lomb 32% and IFF 30%.

Tiger Global cut Alphabet 42%, TSMC 36%, Sea 43%, Lam 31% and Applied Materials 26%, and added Cerebras (+48% to $790M), Danaher (+178%), Intel (+30% to $667M) and a new $237M Ferrari stake. Nvidia is its largest holding at $2.74BN.
Trian's 13F fell from $4.23BN to $2.60BN because the $1.33BN Janus Henderson stake left the filing after Trian and General Catalyst took the asset manager private at $52 a share.

SoftBank bought nothing and sold little. The unchanged 86.96M-share Intel stake fell in value from $12.14BN to $10.45BN (64% of the book), accounting for most of the drop in its 13F from $18.17BN to $16.26BN.

Mid-size activists and value funds: Starboard more than doubled Flowserve and added Knife River and Shake Shack. Engaged exited Freshpet and BlackLine and added Cognex, Yeti and VF. Jana sold Markel and Everpure and added Casella Waste and Modine. Greenlight added PG&E (to 10.0M shares) and Comcast (+110%) and exited PayPal, WBD and StubHub. Paulson added to Madrigal and opened PVH.
crypto_views: Situational Awareness cut bitcoin-miner and AI-hosting exposure: IREN -94%, CleanSpark -75%, Bitdeer -44%, and Core Scientific, Riot and Applied Digital sold outright.
Lone Pine sold Bitdeer outright and cut Hut 8 67% and TeraWulf 56%. Tiger Global sold Applied Digital, Cipher Digital and Core Scientific.

Viking opened Applied Digital ($257M) and TeraWulf positions, and Glenview added Core Scientific ($25M). Senator opened Grayscale Ethereum Staking ETF calls ($10M). BlueCrest terminated iShares Bitcoin Trust puts and TeraWulf.
risk_factors: A 13F shows only US-listed longs and options at Sept. 30, before October's selloff, with no shorts, bonds, currencies, commodities or non-US listings, so it understates hedges and post-quarter moves.
Reported 13F value changes mix price moves and share count changes. Several drops (Intel at SoftBank, GE at TCI, Vertiv at Omega) came from price alone on unchanged share counts.

Share counts for Tiger Global, D1, Viking, Altimeter, Third Point, Baupost, Glenview, Discovery and Senator in the scorecard are approximate. Options are shown at the value of underlying shares, not premium or net exposure.
charts_described: Bar chart 'Who Shrank And Who Didn't: Change In Reported 13F Value, Q3 vs Q2 2026 (%)' ranges from -92% (Situational Awareness) to +21% (Pershing Square), with Nvidia, Trian and Jana among the larger decliners and Icahn, Paulson, Glenview and Appaloosa among the filers with flat to rising reported value.
vol_and_positioning: Index hedging by put buyers: Senator S&P 500 ETF puts rose from 239,500 to 626,000 shares ($179M to $477M notional), Corvex opened $191M of SPY puts, Third Point raised SPY puts +52% to $47M, Soros opened XOP puts ($328M) and raised Energy Select SPDR puts to $670M notional.

Index hedge unwinds: BlueCrest cut S&P 500 puts 94% and Glenview closed $194M of SPY puts. Senator closed $157M of Nasdaq 100 (QQQ) puts. Altimeter bought SMH (VanEck Semiconductor ETF) puts over 840,000 shares ($512M notional) while Glenview opened $48M of SMH puts.
Long call bets on equity beta: BlueCrest SPY calls rose from $22M to $648M notional (23% of its reported book). Druckenmiller closed $487M of ETF calls (RSP, EWZ, IWM, SPY).

Scorecard buyer-to-seller counts among the filers shown: Amazon 7 buyers vs 7 sellers, Meta 7/5, Alphabet 5/8, Nvidia 5/2, TSMC 4/6, Intel 5/1, Micron 4/1, SpaceX 4/4, Broadcom 0/3, Nebius 0/3, Visa 1/4, Uber 2/3 (as printed in the scorecard footer).

Crowding in the largest positions: SpaceX is 55% of D1's book, 41% of Nvidia's, Intel is 64% of SoftBank's and 40% of Nvidia's, CVR Energy and Icahn Enterprises are 86% of Icahn's, and GE Aerospace, Visa, Moody's, S&P Global and Alphabet are 85% of TCI's reported value.
